key_insight: ATLAS learns a diffusion-based sampler for amorphous materials that directly generates Boltzmann-distributed structures from an energy function, enabling efficient sampling, thermodynamic estimation, and inverse design.
engineering_relevance: This could accelerate discovery and optimization of metallic glasses and other disordered materials by replacing costly equilibration and brute-force search with a reusable, composition-general sampler.
method: Equivariant graph neural network parameterizes a diffusion process over atomic structures.
Uses time reversal of diffusion to estimate free energies, entropies, and other observables efficiently.
Supports composition-amortized pretraining and steering toward target properties with optional LLM-guided search.
evidence_signal: On 2D Kob-Andersen systems, ATLAS matches parallel-tempering MCMC distributions and thermodynamic quantities with below 0.2% free-energy error in the low-temperature glass regime using over 500-fold fewer energy evaluations.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the quality and cost of the target energy function or interatomic potential, especially when scaling to new chemistries or expensive oracle evaluations.
paper_title: ATLAS: A Foundation Neural Sampler for Amorphous Materials
